newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH MINISTRY TO DISCUSS GAS SUPPLY PLAN THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: CZECH MINISTRY TO DISCUSS GAS SUPPLY PLAN THURSDAY.

text.p: The Czech industry and trade ministry on Wednesday called a news conference for Thursday in which Minister Vladimir Dlouhy is to discuss diversification of natural gas supplies and other issues.

Ministry spokesman Miroslav Konvalina said the conference at 1 p.m. (1200 gmt) would also include a discussion of the pace of economic growth, the state budget deficit, as well as energy price deregulation and disposing of nuclear waste.
On February 21, Dlouhy said that his ministry had finalised a plan gas supplies, which are now solely from Russia, and would submit it to cabinet within two weeks.
Konvalina said on Wednesday that the ministry also would host Norway's industrial affairs minister Grete Knudsen when she makes an official visit on March 18.
He declined to comment on whether her visit was connected to the decision on natural gas supplies.

The ministry has said it was discussing four options for new gas supplies: * Purchasing all gas from Russia's Gazprom, using two different shipping routes, with a long-term agreement until 2016 and price guarantees until 1998. * Purchasing some Russian gas indirectly through Dutch company Nederlandse Gasunie NV, and Germany's Wintershall, a subsidiary of BASF. Gasunie would start supplies in 1998, delivering up to two billion cubic metres in 2005, with the agreement lasting until 2014. In case of a fall in Russian supplies, Gasunie would deliver its own gas through Wingas, a joint venture of Wintershall and Gazprom.

Wintershall offers a similar scheme, with deliveries through Wingas starting on January 1 next year, rising to one billion cubic metres in 2000, under a deal which would last until 2016. Negotiations with these firms are in the stage of initiating a supply contract. * Finalising an agreement for Norwegian gas, which has already had preliminary approval for supplies between 1997-2017. * A limited purchase from Mobil Europe Gas Inc, Germany's Brigitta Erdgas und Erdoel (BEB) and British Gas Plc. The Czech Republic consumes around eight to nine billion cubic metres of gas per year, but volumes are expected to rise to some 12-13 billion cubic metres by the turn of the century.
